newsitem.title: UK: One Brent date clocked, three others kept - trade. [corrected 18:15 gmt]
newsitem.headline: One Brent date clocked, three others kept - trade. [corrected 18:15 gmt]

text.p: One of the Brent dates nominated on Friday were clocked, while three others were kept from the paper chains ahead of the five o'clock deadline by trading companies, dealers said. (Corrects number of cargoes clocked and kept.)
One cargo loading July 5-7 was clocked to Spanish oil company Repsol, while the other due on the same dates was kept by trading house J.Aron.
A cargo due July 6-8 was clocked to trader Nova, while Wall Street trader Phibro kept the Brent due July 7-9.
Brent cargoes are traded on a paper, or forward market until the 1700 London time deadline on the nearest trading day 15 days before their assigned loading date.
A trading company is clocked when it is left with a cargo which has changed from paper to physical at the deadline and therefore can no longer be passed on as part of pre-sold paper cargo deals.
